related_resources.reason: Chapters 66–72: Hefei, Hanzhong and the ascent of Liu Bei.
Early sources on the Hanzhong campaign and Cao Cao.
Late-Ming textual development and historical narration of dynastic legitimacy.

witness.note: 074000 identifies the surviving 1522 Jiajing printing; its 1494 preface does not prove an unchanged complete novel in 1494. The later received 120-chapter Mao recension remains distinct.

creators.name: Luo Guanzhong
creators.note: Work attribution; distinguish the received text and its transmission from a securely identified single historical author.

description: Traces Liu Bei’s Hanzhong campaign against Cao Cao, the changing fortunes of Guan Yu on the northern frontier and the simultaneous threats that leave the rival kingdoms stretched thin.
